statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the number of integer triples (i,j,k) such that 0 <= i < j <= k < n and arr[i] ^ arr[i+1] ^ ... ^ arr[j-1] = arr[j] ^ arr[j+1] ^ ... ^ arr[k], where ^ denotes bitwise exclusive-or. Equivalently, r is the cardinality of the set of all such triples.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The slice arr is 0-indexed and satisfies 1 <= n <= 300, and for every t with 0 <= t < n, arr[t] is an integer with 1 <= arr[t] <= 10^8. All arithmetic in this specification is exact mathematical integer arithmetic.

statement: Let P[0] = 0 and, for 1 <= t <= n, let P[t] = arr[0] ^ arr[1] ^ ... ^ arr[t-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = sum over all integer pairs (a,b) with 0 <= a < b <= n and P[a] = P[b] of (b - a - 1). Pairs with b = a + 1 contribute 0; if there is no such pair, the sum is 0.
